title: Sharp exponential rates for permanent-on-top and anomalous boson bunching at fixed rank
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. The permanent of a positive semidefinite matrix A is always an eigenvalue of its Schur power matrix Π(A), an n! by n! matrix indexed by permutations. The permanent-on-top conjecture (Soules, 1966) asserted that it is the largest eigenvalue; Shchesnovich disproved it in 2016. This release determines how large the ratio ||Π(A)||/per A can become when the rank d of A is fixed and the order n grows.

Results. (1) At every fixed rank the ratio grows exponentially with a sharp base: eHd-1/d for complex matrices and 2exp{ψ(d/2)-ψ(1)}/d for real ones. The base is e/2 ≈ 1.36 at complex rank two and e2/6 ≈ 1.23 at real rank three, and both tend to eγ ≈ 1.78. (2) The best constant c* in ||Π(A)|| ≤ (c*)n per A satisfies eγ ≤ c* ≤ e1+γ (the upper bound is due to Anari, Gurvits, Oveis Gharan and Saberi), and eγ is the exact asymptotic rate when the rank grows more slowly than √n. An explicit finite bound holds at every order and rank. (3) Balanced permanental compounds have the same sharp bases, so an inequality stated by Pate for 0/1 vectors fails exponentially. (4) In the standard lossless model of partially distinguishable photons, the enhancement of multimode bunching has the same sharp bases; two output modes and polarisation give base e/2. With the six standard polarisations the model enhancement is 62731/28800 ≈ 2.18 at twelve photons and exceeds 24,000 at sixty photons. (5) Configurations attain the full base only if their directions become equidistributed.

Credit and limits. The complex value of the key mixed-pure product gap and its sharpness are due to Yuan and Parrilo (building on Pappas and Révész); the link from the Schur power to that gap uses the postselection technique of Christandl, König and Renner. New here: the link, the real constant, the fixed-rank rates, the lower bound c* ≥ eγ, and the compound, optical and rigidity consequences. The rates are asymptotic; whether c* = eγ is open; the optical values are exact predictions of the standard model, not experiments, and the absolute probabilities are small (about 3×10-5 at twelve photons).

Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF), one Python program (verify_exp_rates.py, 28 checks in exact or declared-tolerance arithmetic) with its JSON output, the bibliography, a machine-readable index, a research-gate record, a review summary, a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Companion release: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24509057.

Assurance. Written proofs with computational checks. Internal AI-assisted review only: a combined five-perspective Claude review, clean replays, one revision round with extensions, a re-review and a proof audit of new and rewritten proofs. No Astra/Codex review took place. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
